summary: A text field for a search query: role="searchbox", Enter submits, Escape clears, and a clear button once there is something to clear. Input's box and sizes.
useWhen: the user types to search or filter a list, a table or a page — the search above a DataTable, the filter at the top of a Sidebar
the query is free text that narrows what is shown, not a value chosen from a list

useInstead.when: the typed text picks one value from a known list — an assignee, a country
useInstead.why: a combobox commits a choice and offers the options; a search field commits a query and offers nothing

useInstead.when: the user is looking for a page or an action anywhere in the product
useInstead.why: that is global and keyboard-first; a SearchField searches the content in front of it

useInstead.when: it is ordinary text entry — a name, an email — that happens to be used for lookup later
useInstead.why: announcing a searchbox promises search behaviour: Escape clears, Enter searches

composition.note: Filter as the user types with `onChange`, or search on Enter with `onSubmit` — pick one per field and say which in the placeholder or label. In a table toolbar, give it `aria-label` naming what it searches.
composition.example: <SearchField aria-label="Search agents" placeholder="Search by name or purpose" value={query} onChange={setQuery} />

sm.use: toolbars, table headers and Sidebar filters, beside small Buttons

lg.use: a page whose main task is searching

guarantees: the input is role="searchbox" and type="search", so it is announced as a search field
Escape clears the query; a second Escape is left for whatever contains the field, so a search in a dialog clears before it closes
Enter calls onSubmit with the query
the clear button is named by React Aria in the user's language, appears only when there is something to clear, and returns focus to the field
the clear button is out of the tab order on purpose: Escape is the keyboard's way to clear, and an extra tab stop in every search box costs every keyboard user a keystroke
the browser's own cancel button is hidden, so there are never two
requires: `label`, or an `aria-label` naming what is searched when no visible label is rendered — "Search" alone does not say what
notes: When filtering as the user types, announce the result count with a polite live region near the results. The field cannot know how many results its query produced; the list does.

antiPatterns.dont: <Input type="search"> with a magnifier as leadingIcon
antiPatterns.why: it looks the same and has none of the behaviour: no searchbox role, no Escape to clear, no labelled clear button
a placeholder disappears once the user types, and is not a reliable accessible name. Pass `aria-label` or `label`

antiPatterns.dont: a separate Search button beside a field that already filters as you type
antiPatterns.why: it teaches the user that nothing happens until they press it, and it does nothing when they do
